CHIPBOOST

Qwen3-8B kernel optimization on Trainium: model alone and referee-guided runs. V1, P1's v2, Qwen + P1 fixes and P3's v2 to v5 are shown separately; template random search uses an expert prior. A run seeded with the verified 1.517x candidate would be a different prior from start-kernel trials; speedups remain relative to the original baseline. A speedup counts only if the referee verifies it: correct on the chip and on unseen shapes, and faster than the noise.

Feedback decides whether the loop works

One dot per run of Qwen3-8B (8 attempts each), from the start kernel. Green: the run produced a kernel the referee verified faster on the chip and correct on unseen shapes.

Correct on shapes it never saw

Speedup over the start kernel at 6 held-out shapes with hostile inputs. Red: wrong at that shape (bf16 ulps against a limit of 4).

Block tuning: +35% over AWS's default

Every legal block setting of AWS's optimised matmul, timed on the chip. Each random-search run's best ranks #1, #3, #4.

A referee you can trust

Squares: planted cheats, by result; circles: honest kernels that must be accepted. Every candidate runs in a sandboxed process; timing is interleaved A/B on the device clock.

P1 red teamc1a_zerosCaughtwrites zerossimulatorat sim (256, 512, 1024): OUTPUT IS 100% ZEROS while the reference is not. Check that every computed tile is copied all the way out: PSUM to SBUF with nisa.tensor_copy, then SBUF to the returned tensor with nisa.dma_copy, for every tile of the loop and not only the last one.
